items.title: Céline Dion Makes Triumphant Return to the Stage in Paris for First Concert in Six Years: Setlist + Videos
items.summary:
Céline Dion performed a full concert for the first time in more than six years on Saturday, September 12th, opening her residency at Paris La Défense Arena before a sold-out crowd of more than 30,000. It was her first show since she was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome in 2022, a neurological condition that causes progressive stiffness in the muscles of the torso, arms and legs and had made performing impossible.

Dion opened with the French-language "On ne change pas" and was visibly emotional, wiping away tears during a standing ovation before moving through "Encore un soir," "Tout l'or des hommes," "Because You Loved Me" and Jennifer Rush's "The Power of Love." The show ran four acts and 26 songs, split between her French and English catalogs, plus a four-song encore.

Consequence reported that the set included three live debuts — "The Chase," "Dansons" and "Je chanterai" — along with the first complete performance of "Ne bouge pas" since 2003 and the first live rendition of "Les derniers seront les premiers" since 2009. The second act paired "My Heart Will Go On" with "Beauty and the Beast" and then ran a medley from Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" into "I'm Alive," "That's the Way It Is" and "Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)."

The main set closed with "Courage," "Love Can Move Mountains," "The Prayer" and "It's All Coming Back to Me Now," capped by an operatic reading of Catalani's "Ebben? Ne andrò lontana." The encore took in "All by Myself," "Pour que tu m'aimes encore" and "S'il suffisait d'aimer" before ending on "Des milliers de baisers."

Dion announced the residency in March, when the question of whether she could perform live again was still open. "This year, I'm getting the best birthday gift of my life," she said in a video message at the time. "I'm getting the chance to see you, to perform for you once again in Paris, beginning in September! I'm feeling good, I'm strong, I'm feeling excited, obviously a little nervous, but most of all, I'm grateful to all of you!"

She returns to La Défense Arena on Wednesday, September 16th for the second of ten shows, with further dates on September 19th, 23rd, 26th and 30th, and October 3rd, 7th, 10th and 14th. Another run at the same venue follows next May.

items.title: Celine Dion returns to the stage after battling rare illness
items.summary:
Céline Dion has returned to performing, opening a 16-show residency at the Plenitude Arena in Paris. The run marks the Canadian singer's return to the stage after a rare illness kept her away from live performance.

NPR Music reported that the entire residency is sold out. That covers every date in the series, not just the opening night.

The residency is Dion's first sustained stretch of concerts since her health forced her off the road, and it is confined to the single Paris venue.

items.title: Drake Reveals ‘Fear of Missing Out’ Teaser, Says Project Is a ‘Not So Short Film’
items.summary:
Drake posted a teaser on Saturday for "Fear of Missing Out," clarifying what the long-teased project actually is: a film. In the Instagram caption he described it as a "not so short film" that was "directed and scored by the family," with a release set for September 15.

The clip runs on a single image — a man, presumably Drake, cutting across flat ocean water in a neon green speedboat — over a woman's narration. "What if I told you there were two versions of your life?" she says. "In one, you avoid risk and withhold love. You feel like you've gone missing from yourself. You look for something you can't find. In the other version of your life, you find it." A title card follows.

Variety reported that fans had spent months guessing whether FOMO would turn out to be an album, a music video or a tour. Drake first revealed the title and release date on September 3, leaving the format unexplained until the teaser landed.

The project follows an unusually dense release stretch. Drake's last major drop was the long-rumored "Iceman," which arrived alongside two surprise records, "Habibti" and "Maid of Honour" — 43 songs in total, with contributions from Future, 21 Savage, Sexyy Red, Qendresa, Molly Santana, Central Cee, Popcaan, PartyNextDoor, Loe Shimmy, Iconic Savvy and Stunna Sandy.

Elaborate rollouts are standard practice for him. While promoting "Iceman," the five-time Grammy winner installed a 25-foot ice sculpture in a Toronto parking lot. "Fear of Missing Out" arrives September 15.

items.title: ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’ Review: Mahershala Ali Is a Marvel in a Gripping Crime Film With a Big, Aching Heart
items.summary:
"Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother," written and directed by Bassam Tariq and starring Mahershala Ali, premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival as a Special Presentation ahead of its September 25 release. The 102-minute crime film also features Giancarlo Esposito, John Cho, Tramell Tillman, Abubakr Ali, Laith Nakli, Tiffany Boone, Adia, Jahleel Kamara, John Henry Ward and Shakirah DeMesier.

Ali plays Latif, a former Marine who has kept killing stateside as a contractor for a wealthy, corrupt employer named Mike, played by Nakli. The work has estranged him from his suburban brother Talib (Tillman) and his disapproving father-in-law Abdul Malik (Esposito). When his wife Khadijah (DeMesier) dies suddenly, he is left as sole parent to three children.

The film's engine is domestic rather than criminal. Latif's adolescent daughter Fatiha (Adia) presses him with questions he'd rather not answer, his devout son Qadir (Kamara) forces him to face his lapsed faith, and his infant daughter Aziza can't digest formula, turning his days into a search for breast milk. A man comfortable as a provider has to learn to nurture.

In its review, The Hollywood Reporter called the film "worthy of its star's vast talent," arguing that Tariq has given Ali his first leading role commensurate with his abilities since "Moonlight" — and noting that Ali elevated "Green Book" beyond what the film around him earned, while the Blade project fans anticipated never materialized.

The review singles out Cho, playing against type as Pastor Kwan, another troubled veteran who presents himself as a man of faith while pursuing power alone. Gold teeth, cowboy hat, guns, a manufactured culture war — the character reads as a distinctly American villain, and the scenes he shares with Ali are described as the film's high points.

Tariq's central achievement, per the review, is a Black Muslim protagonist drawn tenderly, with family and faith as anchors rather than as menace. The film opens in theaters September 25.

items.title: Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October
items.summary:
Comedian Dyon Brooks, who performs as Mojo Brookzz, will premiere his first stand-up special, "I Know You Lying," on Netflix worldwide on October 6. Deadline reported the date exclusively.

Brooks filmed the hour at Atlanta's Center Stage Theatre in December 2025. Mike "Homeless Pimp" Lavin directed, with Lavin, Jason Nower and John-J Sheridan producing for 3 Nuts Studios, and Brooks, Bernie Cahill and Grant Pennel of Activist Artists Management serving as executive producers. The subject matter has not been disclosed.

The special borrows its title from Brooks' 2025 headlining tour, which sold more than 100,000 tickets across 40 cities. That followed his 2024 Unhand Me Now Tour, which moved more than 65,000 tickets — a two-year climb from clubs to theaters to arenas.

He is currently out on the 42-date Outta Pocket Tour, his largest to date, covering the U.S., Hawaii and Europe. The sold-out run includes two homecoming dates at Chicago's Wintrust Arena and two nights at New York's Beacon Theatre in November as part of the New York Comedy Festival.

Brooks has also sold out his 2026 slot at Netflix Is a Joke Fest and appears in Tyler Perry's series "Miss Governor," which logged multiple weeks in Netflix's Top 10. A regular partner of the Chicago Bears during the NFL season, he turns up next in "Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story" from Hallmark, the NFL and Skydance Sports in December.
